In brief: This week will see a prolonged period of wet weather in Abuja, with high chances of rain on each day, as a low-pressure system maintains its grip on the region, leading to increased humidity and reduced temperatures. The current weather conditions in Abuja, with a temperature of 22°C and a feels-like temperature of 25°C, are a precursor to the wet week ahead. The high humidity of 98% is already making the air feel heavy, and this trend is expected to continue throughout the week. The wind direction, currently blowing at 12 km/h, will play a crucial role in shaping the weather patterns over the next few days. As we head into the week, the UV index will remain low, a consequence of the thick cloud cover that will dominate the skies.
### Monday The low-pressure system that has been influencing the weather in Abuja will continue to do so on Monday, leading to a high chance of rain. Models suggest that the rain will be most intense in the morning hours, with a gradual decrease in intensity as the day wears on. The high temperature will be around 28°C, while the low will be 21°C. The humidity will remain high, ranging from 80% to 90% throughout the day. The wind direction will shift from northwesterly to southeasterly, leading to an influx of moist air from the Gulf of Guinea. This will result in increased precipitation, particularly in low-lying areas such as Gwarinpa and the airport road. The heavy rain on Monday will lead to flooding in some areas, particularly those with poor drainage systems. Residents in Maitama and Wuse should be prepared for possible flooding, especially during the morning hours when the rain is expected to be heaviest. The good news is that the rain will bring some relief from the heat, and the feels-like temperature will be significantly lower than the actual temperature. The cloud cover will also reduce the UV index, making it a good day to be outdoors without worrying about sunburn. The rain on Monday will also have an impact on traffic, particularly on the Nnamdi Azikiwe Expressway. The road is already prone to congestion, and the wet weather will only exacerbate the situation. Residents should plan their journeys accordingly, leaving early to account for potential delays. The traffic congestion will be particularly bad during the morning and evening rush hours, when the rain is expected to be heaviest.
### Tuesday The low-pressure system will continue to dominate the weather on Tuesday, leading to another day of heavy rain. The high temperature will be slightly lower than on Monday, around 25°C, while the low will remain the same at 21°C. The humidity will be even higher than on Monday, ranging from 90% to 95% throughout the day. The wind direction will remain southeasterly, bringing in even more moist air from the Gulf of Guinea. The rain will be intense, with precipitation accumulation expected to range from 20mm to 30mm. The heavy rain on Tuesday will lead to increased flooding in low-lying areas, particularly those near the Garki and Aso Rock areas. Residents should be prepared for possible power outages, as the heavy rain can lead to flash flooding and subsequent disruptions to the power supply. The good news is that the rain will continue to bring relief from the heat, and the feels-like temperature will be significantly lower than the actual temperature. The cloud cover will also reduce the UV index, making it a good day to be outdoors without worrying about sunburn. The impact of the heavy rain on Tuesday will be felt across the city, with many areas experiencing disruptions to their daily activities. The National Assembly complex, located in the heart of the city, may experience flooding, particularly in the parking areas. The nearby areas, including the Three Arms Zone, may also experience flooding, particularly during the morning and evening rush hours.
### Wednesday The low-pressure system will begin to weaken on Wednesday, leading to a slight decrease in the intensity of the rain. The high temperature will be around 27°C, while the low will remain the same at 21°C. The humidity will still be high, ranging from 80% to 90% throughout the day. The wind direction will shift from southeasterly to northeasterly, leading to a decrease in the influx of moist air from the Gulf of Guinea. The precipitation accumulation is expected to range from 10mm to 20mm. The decrease in the intensity of the rain on Wednesday will lead to a slight improvement in the traffic situation, particularly on the Nnamdi Azikiwe Expressway. However, residents should still be prepared for possible delays, particularly during the morning and evening rush hours. The flooding in low-lying areas will also begin to subside, particularly in areas such as Gwarinpa and the airport road. The weakening of the low-pressure system on Wednesday will also lead to a slight increase in the UV index, as the cloud cover begins to clear. Residents should still be prepared for possible rain showers, particularly during the morning and evening hours. The feels-like temperature will still be significantly lower than the actual temperature, making it a good day to be outdoors without worrying about heat stress. ### Thursday The low-pressure system will continue to weaken on Thursday, leading to a further decrease in the intensity of the rain. The high temperature will be around 28°C, while the low will remain the same at 21°C. The humidity will still be high, ranging from 80% to 90% throughout the day. The wind direction will remain northeasterly, leading to a continued decrease in the influx of moist air from the Gulf of Guinea. The precipitation accumulation is expected to range from 5mm to 10mm. The decrease in the intensity of the rain on Thursday will lead to a significant improvement in the traffic situation, particularly on the Nnamdi Azikiwe Expressway. Residents should still be prepared for possible delays, particularly during the morning and evening rush hours. The flooding in low-lying areas will also continue to subside, particularly in areas such as Gwarinpa and the airport road. The weakening of the low-pressure system on Thursday will also lead to a further increase in the UV index, as the cloud cover continues to clear. Residents should still be prepared for possible rain showers, particularly during the morning and evening hours. The feels-like temperature will still be significantly lower than the actual temperature, making it a good day to be outdoors without worrying about heat stress. In conclusion, the prolonged period of wet weather in Abuja will require residents to be prepared for possible flooding, disruptions to their daily activities, and reduced temperatures. The key takeaway for residents is to plan their journeys accordingly, leaving early to account for potential delays, and to be prepared for possible power outages and flooding in low-lying areas.
